text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia on Tuesday said it was withdrawing its bid for a proposed merger with mortgage bank Stadshypotek that is also under a rival bid from Handelsbanken.

Skandia and Stadshypotek, which is 34 percent state-owned, proposed a merger on November 25 but this offer was quashed by a 22.9 billion crown takeover bid last Thursday by commercial bank Handelsbanken that received governmental approval.
"Skandia believes that it is unlikely that the public offer of November 25 will achieve its goal of acquiring more than 90 percent of the shares in Stadshypotek," Skandia said in a statement.
"As as result the board has today resolved to withdraw its bid for Stadshypotek and to cancel the extraordinary general meeting scheduled for Thursday, December 19."
The Skandia proposal valued Stadshypotek, the country's largest mortgage lender with a third of the market, at around 21 billion crowns.
The government has said its aim was to get the highest possible prices for the current sale of the stake's holding in Stadshypotek.
Skandia said it remained committed to its strategic goals to expand in the Nordic insurance and savings product sector and to be global leader in the area of unit linked assurance.

"Skandia will continue to explore new opportunities for expansion in the Nordic markets through acquisitions and joint ventures and will continue its global expansion of the unit linked operations through the Assurance & Financial Services, AFS, unit," the company said.
"Skandia has adequate capital resources to fund near and medium term growth."

The company said to the extent that external capital was needed for future growth, Skandia would take advantage of market opportunities as and when deemed appropriate on terms suitable for its sharesholders.
